reading.body:
DartPoints Greenville publishes 2.5 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 2.5 MW is roughly 62 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it is roughly 250 racks. The operator has not published certifications, redundancy tier, or power usage effectiveness on the page this site read, so no further qualification of what the facility can host can be derived from the data.

South Carolina has 14 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish a megawatt figure. Those 4 together total 6.6 MW of published IT capacity. DartPoints Greenville, at 2.5 MW, ranks first among them by that measure, meaning it accounts for roughly 38 percent of all published IT capacity in the state on this site's current read.

That ranking reflects the thinness of published data in South Carolina more than it reflects the absolute scale of the facility. 2.5 MW is a modest figure by the standards of purpose-built AI infrastructure, where single training clusters routinely require tens of megawatts. A campus of this size is more plausibly relevant to inference workloads, edge deployment, or regional enterprise compute than to large-scale model training, though the operator has not published the power density or cooling specifications that would confirm any of those uses.
